newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO SAYS GRANTS TWO ENERGY PERMITS.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO SAYS GRANTS TWO ENERGY PERMITS.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said on Wednesday it granted two energy permits to foreign companies.

Finnish Metra Oy Ab unit Wartsila Diesel de Mexico was given a permit to build a power station for self-generation on Cozumel island, the CRE said in a statement. "The power station will include four internal combustion motor-generators and will have a local capacity of 26 megawatts. Annually it will produce close to 136 gigawatt hours and will consume approximately one million cubic feet of fuel oil daily," the CRE said.
The $15 million new plant should will help supply electricity to the popular resort island, the CRE said.
The commission also said it granted a natural gas permit to the Mexican unit of U.S. Igasamex USA Ltd Integrated Services.
With the permit, the company can build and operated a 1.5 mile-long and 4.5 inch diameter pipiline in the central Mexican state of Guanajuato, and transport natural gas to two firms.
"The system will have a capacity of up to 12.7 million cubic feet per day," the CRE said. "Igasamex shall provide open access, not unduly discriminatory, service on its system."

Mexico is selling rights to build new power plants to help satisfy a growing domestic electricity demand and is auctioning concessions to distribute, transport and store natural gas. All exploration and production and refining remains in the hands of monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
